chunks: And it is narrated from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever seeks sustenance through its lawful means and is overcome, then let him borrow in reliance upon Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and upon His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the Divine source of provision
key_terms.رَسُولِهِ: His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.فَغُلِبَ: he was overcome or unable to cope
key_terms.فَلْيَسْتَقْرِضْ: then let him take a loan

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they seek halal livelihood but still cannot meet their needs?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that when a person seeks livelihood through halal means yet is unable to manage, borrowing is permitted as a recourse. It frames such borrowing as being undertaken with trust in Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, reflecting both lawful striving and reliance upon God.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3684 - It is narrated from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (as), who said: "
Whoever seeks sustenance through lawful means and is overcome, let him borrow in the name of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family)."
